name: dashboard-sidebar
title: Dashboard Sidebar
description: Responsive application sidebar with searchable navigation, active destinations, and a mobile-drawer-ready structure for multi-section product interfaces.
useWhen: A SaaS dashboard, admin panel, or internal tool has several primary destinations.
Navigation should remain available on desktop while changing to a drawer or disclosure on mobile.
Users benefit from filtering or searching a larger set of navigation destinations.
avoidWhen: A marketing page has only a few top-level links — use a header navigation instead.
The product has one focused workflow with no persistent destination switching.
Navigation must display more than one independent hierarchy without a defined information architecture.
responsiveBehavior: The sidebar remains persistent beside content on desktop. On small viewports it must move into a labelled drawer or disclosure triggered from the application header, with focus returned to the trigger on close.
accessibility: Wrap destinations in a nav landmark with an accessible label such as 'Primary navigation'.
Mark the current destination with aria-current='page' and do not rely only on its visual fill color.
The mobile drawer trigger needs an accessible name, aria-expanded state, and keyboard-operable close control.
Search input needs a visible label or an equivalent accessible name.

variants.title: Searchable navigation
variants.description: Responsive dashboard sidebar with a navigation search field, active destination state, and a content area that demonstrates the intended application-shell relationship.
accessibility: Use aria-current='page' on the active link and retain a visible focus style for every destination.
When rendered in a drawer, trap focus only while the drawer is open and restore focus to its trigger on close.
